boardTitle: B168 and DT349: numbers for the portions you choose, the Plate's PD card, the cooking at Start cooking

B168.title: The numbers under One portion show the whole recipe

opportunity.from: Seen while drawing B166, 23 November 2026, on Lazy Burek's page; Coach Milan 24 November 07:04: yes, its own ticket, we need to fix that.
opportunity.job: Read what one portion of my recipe holds.
opportunity.kind: Says something not true: the table under One portion shows the whole recipe.
opportunity.why_now: B166 made the table readable, so its numbers are now read.

B168.problem: On a recipe that makes 4 portions, the PD card says One portion, 549 kcal and 224 g. Its numbers say Total 897 g and 2,194 kcal, fat 135 g: the whole recipe. The Nutrition table below says 1 portion, 224 g. Two places on one page disagree about one portion.
B168.story: When I read the numbers of a recipe, I want to choose how many portions they count, one or the whole recipe, without changing what I cook, so that I can trust what I plan and eat.
B168.now: The card says One portion, 549 kcal · 23.3 g protein · 224 g. Its numbers are handed the whole recipe: Total 897 g, 2,194 kcal. Cook it's − 4 portions + sits under the card and changes only the foods to cook.
B168.proposed: Numbers for − 1 portion +, right above the PD card: how many portions the card and its numbers count, from 1 portion to All 4 portions. It opens at one portion each time and is not saved: reading changes nothing in the recipe. The card's rows and its numbers follow; PD and the letters stay, they are rates. The cooking has its own − and + (DT349), and neither changes the other.
B168.looked_at: − and + inside the card's title (07:55): not chosen, no more navigation in the card (07:58). The card following Cook it (08:05, the variant): not chosen; reading the numbers would change the batch, which is saved with the recipe (13:53: separate the whole recipe and cooking from the portion calculation of macros). The card always one portion (07:10): not chosen; the whole recipe's numbers would be lost.
B168.short: Numbers for − 1 portion + above the PD card: what the card and its numbers count, not saved; with DT349 in one release, 0.3.193

B168.checks: Full, for B168 and DT349 together: the PD card becomes one component the Plate uses too, and Cook it moves; new words. All walkthroughs, about 41 minutes, with a message at 50% and 90%; the new walkthrough for B168 AC1 to AC6 and DT349 AC1 to AC6; the German sweep.

DT349.title: The recipe page: the Plate's PD card, and the cooking at Start cooking

opportunity.from: Coach Milan 24 November 2026, 07:42, looking at the board B168; 13:44 to 13:54, brainstorm on the − and +.
opportunity.job: Read a recipe's numbers the way I read a plate, and cook the batch I choose.
opportunity.kind: Did not find it or did not understand it: the recipe's PD card looks different from the Plate's; Cook it looks like a button and sits by the numbers, which it does not change.
opportunity.why_now: B168 makes the card count a chosen number of portions, so the card and the cooking need their own places.

DT349.problem: The recipe page's PD card has its own layout: one small line for kcal, protein and grams, its numbers inside the card. On the Plate the same card has rows and opens its numbers under it. Cook it, under the card, looks like a call to action and says 1 portions.
DT349.story: When I open a recipe, I want its PD card to read like the Plate's and the cooking to sit where I cook, so that I find each in its place.
DT349.now: Recipe page: PD card (own layout), Cook it card with − 4 portions + under it, Start cooking at the end of the Steps.
DT349.proposed: 1. The recipe page takes the Plate's PD card, one component for both (PdCard): PD with its tap to the scale, the words against your target, Energy, Weight and Protein as rows, the letters; the numbers open under the card. 2. The Cook it card goes; its − 4 portions + moves to Start cooking, saved with the recipe as now, with its lines (As the recipe makes it, Back to 4, as written, the plan's count). It says 1 portion, 2 portions. 3. docs/rules/design.md D8: every PD card is PdCard and opens its numbers under it; design-rules.cjs checks it.
DT349.looked_at: The PD card's layout and B168 on two boards: not chosen, one page redesign (13:51). A food's PD card (FoodCard): not in DT349, unless Coach Milan says.
DT349.short: The recipe page takes the Plate's PD card (PdCard, design rule D8); the cooking's − and + moves to Start cooking; with B168, 0.3.193
